scenario_provenance.archetype_label: Inference: a significance test or confidence interval
validity_rules: one-population proportion test setup only: identify H0 and Ha
H0 uses equality to the hypothesized population proportion p0
Ha direction follows the stated research question: greater than, less than, or different from

sources.note: the item stem's verb must match the scored demand

prompt: A researcher is setting up a one-sample z test for a population proportion. The research question is whether less than 25% of new users abandon the signup process. In a random sample of 180 new users, 37 abandon the signup process. Which pair of hypotheses is appropriate?

options.text: Let p be the true proportion of new users of an app who abandon the signup process. H0: p = 0.25; Ha: p < 0.25.
Let p-hat be the sample proportion with this trait. H0: p-hat = 0.25; Ha: p-hat < 0.25.

misconception_source.label: Used the sample proportion instead of the population proportion in hypotheses

sources.note: one-proportion inference tests a claim about the population proportion p, while p-hat is the sample statistic used as evidence

options.text: Let p be the true proportion of new users of an app who abandon the signup process. H0: p = 0.25; Ha: p > 0.25.

misconception_source.label: Used the wrong direction for the alternative hypothesis

sources.note: the alternative hypothesis direction must match the claim being tested: greater than, less than, or different from the hypothesized proportion

options.text: Let p be the true proportion of new users of an app who abandon the signup process. H0: p < 0.25; Ha: p = 0.25.

misconception_source.label: Put equality in the alternative hypothesis

sources.note: hypothesis tests require null and alternative hypotheses; the null carries the equality case and the alternative carries the research direction
